question: OJC Fund recipients with no BMF match: check the 476 EINs (FY2023-24 Schedule I, $59.3m, 8.2% of OJC's itemised dollars) against the IRS automatic-revocation list and Pub 78 data, and test for EIN keying errors by name match against the BMF; repeat for any church-block recipient that later drops from the BMF
conclusion_affected: Whether any OJC dollars counted outside the church block went to revoked or mis-keyed EINs; recipient-screen error rates at pass-through sponsors
rationale: 8.2% of OJC's Schedule I dollars go to EINs absent from the 2026-11 BMF. They are outside the church block, so the faith share is unaffected, but the share is far above what the top-50 sponsors show and the IRS lists are public and allowed

question: Apply the same Schedule I audit to the other Orthodox high-throughput sponsors (Matbia Charities, The Donors' Fund, Friends of Mosdot Goor, Jewish Communal Fund): share of church-block dollars to school/yeshiva and chesed-fund names, share to DAF sponsors, and overlap with OJC recipients
conclusion_affected: Whether the 42% yeshiva-and-fund share is OJC-specific or common to Orthodox sponsors; robustness of the 27-30% faith share
rationale: OJC sends 25.9% of its block dollars to school/yeshiva names and 16.5% to chesed/relief funds; 74.5% of its block dollars go to recipients that other sponsors (Fidelity 1,119 of them, JCF 294) also pay, so the same recipients recur across sponsors

question: What is the PayPal Charitable Giving Fund to OJC Fund flow ($16.7m FY2023, $27.7m FY2024 on PPGF's Schedule I)? Read both returns' Schedule I purpose text and PPGF's public help pages to establish whether OJC fundholders top up accounts through PayPal, and whether other processors route money into faith DAF sponsors the same way
conclusion_affected: Attribution of OJC's church-block dollars between faith and processor sponsors (currently 7.4% of OJC contributions come from other panel sponsors' grants)
rationale: Panel sponsors paid OJC $54.0m in FY2023-24, 7.4% of its DAF contributions; $44.4m of it is PPGF. Reattributing that share moves the S3 faith share only from 30.2% to 29.7%, but the processor-to-DAF rail itself is undocumented

question: Hand-validate the congregation name rule: draw a seeded sample of 200 church-block recipients (stratified by faith/non-faith sponsor and by fine type) and check each against its own website or state charity record, to estimate the precision of 'congregation', 'school_yeshiva', 'chesed_or_relief_fund' and 'unclassified'
conclusion_affected: The congregations-only faith share (23.0% symmetric, 27.3% OJC-only) depends on a name rule that leaves 17-29% of block dollars unclassified
rationale: The symmetric congregations-only scope keeps only 57% of S3 block dollars; the base rule and the Orthodox-aware rule disagree on 4% of OJC dollars (ministry vs fund) and many Hebrew names are opaque (TOIREM, SIFREI ALGAZI, BINYAN YERUSHLAIM)

question: Groundswell TY2025 Form 990: when it appears in the TEOS index, read Part IV line 6, Schedule D Part I columns (a) and (b) and Part III, to see whether line 6 is corrected to Yes and how fast accounts and assets grow; check whether DAFRC's next dataset adds Groundswell
conclusion_affected: Outside-DAFRC FY2024-25 account totals (24,800 with Groundswell); line-6 false-negative rate
rationale: Its only DAF figures are on an amended TY2024 return answering line 6 No while Schedule D lines 5-6 answer Yes; its own terms (updated 2026-07-06) describe every account as a DAF, so TY2025 should show whether the filing error persists

question: Workplace-platform DAF accounts: build a register of employee-giving platforms whose accounts are DAFs at an affiliated 501(c)(3) (Groundswell, DEED, Visit.org, Benevity/AOGF, YourCause/Blackbaud Giving Fund), with account counts, average balance and whether employer matches are deposited into the employee's account; tag these accounts separately in market account totals
conclusion_affected: How much of DAF account growth is employer-funded micro-accounts rather than traditional donor accounts
rationale: Groundswell's 12,808 accounts are per-employee DAFs averaging $787 with grants averaging at most $172; employer matches go into the employee's DAF and are excluded from the employee's tax receipt, so the employer is the donor of those dollars
